correctness.rationale: The exact drift factorization and Bernstein probability-logarithmic derivative bound the fitness-odds slope strictly by the group-size-controlled Bernstein slope. The mutation-odds logarithmic slope dominates that bound at and above the sharp mutation threshold. A unique transverse crossing follows with the drift globally oriented toward it; the q=1/2 case factors directly. For each q<q_d the explicit positive endpoint-coordination family makes the central equilibrium repelling and forces one more on either side by endpoint signs. Exact symbolic polynomial identities and 144 exact Sturm checks support, but do not replace, the infinite-domain proof.

value.rationale: The universal positive-payoff mutation threshold \(q_d=(d-1)/(2d)\) separates a guaranteed single globally attracting evolutionary composition from the parameter range permitting bistability, for every group size d. This converts payoff-dependent root counting into a structural worst-case theorem with an explicit sharp family, and gives a rigorous control bound for selection–mutation models; it is neither a small numerical improvement nor a known-table recomputation.
